specFirst: This file was written BEFORE the code (todo/todo-agent-new-theme.md; design in todo/analise-agent-new-theme.md). The code is validated against it. Maintenance changes the spec FIRST, then the code.
description: Standalone agent that GENERATES FROM SCRATCH the current project's theme file (l2/skills/theme.ts, contract v1) via an LLM, guided by the shared themeAuthoring meta-skill, with ONE human checkpoint (clarification). It does NOT clone an existing theme and does NOT improve one (backlog). The theme.ts (plus a deterministic theme.html doc/preview) is written as soon as the generation passes its contract gate. Consumed downstream by the molecule agents (New Molecule / Variant / Improve), which read the theme to style each molecule's .less.
principles: Generate, don't clone: v1 authors a NEW theme from a natural-language description + clarification answers. Clone (mode A) and Improve Theme (mode C) are backlog.

Human-in-the-loop, lean: exactly ONE checkpoint (adjust A1, 2026-07-27). It collects ONLY the theme fields the initial prompt did not pin down (dynamic questions with options + recommended defaults); if nothing is missing it is skipped (fast path). There is NO final confirmation screen: the human decides BEFORE generation, and the deterministic contract gate decides after it. A confirm/preview checkpoint (and an adjust loop) is backlog — see todo Fase 8.

Nothing on disk until the gate is green: theme.ts and theme.html are written by t3-generate only after the contract gate passes. A generation that fails the gate twice writes NOTHING, and cancelling the checkpoint writes NOTHING.

Quality is the meta-skill: generation injects l2/aura/molecules/skills/themeAuthoring (the authoring rules distilled from the Variant acceptance tests P3-P10). A generated theme must respect them (geometry is the render's; overlays opaque; primitives not glassified; comments in English; etc.).
Contract-gated: the generated theme.ts must pass the shared validator l2/aura/molecules/shared/vThemeContract.validateVThemeModule before it can be written.

Step is the maintenance unit: 1 folder per step (agent hook, prompt.md when LLM, gate + test, readme, CHANGELOG). helpers/ (nt*) are minimal and owned by this agent; only the theme contract validator is shared.
i18n split: questions/labels/summary are localized (userLanguage detected in t1-plan); the generated theme.ts comments/prose are ALWAYS English (rule P10).

Recovery is deletion: admission stays strict (a project with a theme.ts is refused), so regenerating means deleting/renaming the file. No force/rebuild flag in v1 — it would make clobbering a real project's theme a one-liner.

conventions.input: PROSE is the natural form: @@agentNewTheme <free description of the desired style, e.g. 'a soft neumorphic light theme, brand color #6C5CE7'>. The object form @@agentNewTheme { prompt: '<description>' } is also accepted. Parsing lives in helpers/ntEntry.ntParseEntryPrompt (pure, tested): the source is the runtime-stripped userPrompt argument, our own '@@'/agent-name prefix is removed (the runtime only drops the first space-delimited token, so '@@ agentNewTheme x' still carries the name), and mls.common.safeParseArgs is called ONLY when the text opens an object literal — it THROWS on prose ('Invalid args format, cannot parse.'), which is what broke the prose mention before. A malformed object degrades to prose instead of failing the task. A bare mention (empty prompt) is valid: every field falls to the checkpoint. Test mode receives JSON { prompt }.
conventions.destinationProject: mls.actualProject (the studio's current project). The theme is written to _<dest>_/l2/skills/theme.ts (+ theme.html).
conventions.admission: The project must NOT already have l2/skills/theme.ts (New Theme creates from scratch). If it exists, fail readable with orientation ('this project already has a theme; Improve Theme is not available yet') — never clobber.
conventions.themeContract: contract v1, validated by l2/aura/molecules/shared/vThemeContract.validateVThemeModule: exports themeInfo{name,suffix(starts with '-'),displayName,description,background{kind:'light'|'dark'|'image',css,note}}, skill (4 sections: '## 1. Visual Signature'/'## 2. Tokens'/'## 3. Canonical CSS Rules'/'## 4. Theme Nuances'(opt)), examples[] (start EMPTY).
conventions.themeFields: Canonical fields collected/derived for the theme: name(->suffix), displayName, background.kind(light|dark|image)+css, primary/accent, corners(sharp|rounded|pill), border(none|thin|thick+color), shadow(none|soft|offset), motion(smooth|instant|none), typography(sans|mono|serif + uppercaseLabels?). suffix is NEVER collected — always derived as '-'+name, because the t3 gate requires that. surface/on-surface(text) are DERIVED from background.kind (light bg -> dark text; dark bg -> light text) and NOT asked. background.kind:'image' is accepted only via free-text CSS (no upload in v1).
conventions.freeTextSlot: The fields are coarse enums, so they cannot express exact values ('3px', '4px 4px 0 #000'), signature interactions ('on hover the element slides 2px into its own shadow') or prohibitions ('no blur'). Whenever the checkpoint runs, its LAST question is a free-text slot (field 'extra', options [], allowNotes true) that collects exactly that. helpers/ntAnswers.ntResolveAnswers merges known + answers into one decided field set and concatenates the slot AND every per-question note into one guidance block; t3's prompt states that exact values in the guidance WIN over the coarse field choices. This is what lets a short request approach the precision of a long one. When nothing is missing the checkpoint is skipped and no slot is added (the fast path stays intact).
conventions.clarification: The checkpoint uses the supported pattern (collab_messages.md 'Rendering a checkpoint'): the step agent EMITS a clarification into its OWN interaction.payload (cheap codefast call returning {type:'clarification', json}); beforeClarificationStep mounts the shared widget; a completed result step (the 't2-done' anchor the next step dependsOn) both completes the emitting agent and unlocks downstream. Never a flat clarification in nextSteps; never a wrapper+child. Widgets live in l2/aura/molecules/shared/.
conventions.structuredSummary: t3-generate returns, besides the theme.ts string, a structured summary { name, displayName, background{kind,css}, palette:[{token,label,color}], signature:[{aspect,value}] } persisted to l4. It feeds the deterministic theme.html AND the read-only step view (openStepView on t3 mounts the shared Theme Confirmation widget in readonly mode, so the palette/signature stay inspectable in the chat after the fact).
conventions.writeOnGreenGate: theme.ts and theme.html are written to _<dest>_/l2/skills/ by t3-generate the moment its gate passes, and the .ts is compiled best-effort (the molecule agents import the compiled theme.js). Gate red twice => nothing written.
conventions.draft: l4/agentNewTheme/draft.json = { themeTs, summary } produced by t3 — kept after the write because the structured summary is NOT deterministically recoverable from theme.ts (it feeds theme.html, the read-only step view and a future Improve Theme); l4/agentNewTheme/plan.json = t1 output (known + questions); answers.json = checkpoint answers; trace-<step>-<attempt>.json per step.
conventions.gates: 1 gate = 1 file = 1 .test.ts inside the step folder. t3 gate => 1 retry with errors in context; a 2nd failure FAILS the step and nothing is written.
conventions.doneAnchors: Every step that passes its gate emits a completed result step with planId 't<N>-done'. Downstream depends ONLY on done anchors. t1 has NO anchor (it is the root's own call — the root plants the tree directly), so on the fast path t3-generate is planted as the first runnable step (waiting_human_input, no dependsOn); with the checkpoint it is planted waiting_dependency on 't2-done'. The checkpoint answer result IS the 't2-done' anchor (one completed result both completes the emitting step and unlocks t3). 't3-done' is the TERMINAL anchor: nothing depends on it, it carries the written files, and the task ends there.
conventions.i18n: userLanguage detected in t1-plan drives step titles, questions and labels; the theme.ts content is English. The LLM localizes the plan title and the questions; the fixed UI strings (step titles, widget intro/labels) come from a small pt/en table in the code, falling back to English — the t1 schema deliberately has no titles map.
conventions.modelType: EVERY prompt (prompt.md and inline system prompts) must carry '<!-- modelType: X -->' on its first line, chosen from skills/modelTypes.md. Without it the platform falls back to a cost-based selection and the call dies with '404 Model alias not found or inactive: cost' (1st Studio run, t3-generate).
conventions.v2ExplicitlyOut: No clone, no Improve Theme, no image upload, no multi-theme per project, no final confirmation checkpoint, no adjust loop, no smoke-molecule preview, no force/rebuild overwrite. See todo Fase 8.

folderLayout.agentNewTheme.ts: root: parses { prompt }, admission (no existing theme.ts), creates the task (add-message-ai with the cheap t1-plan call), plants the step tree (t2 only when there are questions; t3 always).
folderLayout.spec.md: human-readable rationale; links to the analysis/control docs
folderLayout.helpers/: ntEntry.ts (mention parsing: prose or { prompt }, pure with an injected arg parser), ntAnswers.ts (known + checkpoint answers -> decided fields + free-text guidance), ntFs.ts (theme file refs/paths, l4 draft/plan/trace read-write, write theme.ts/.html), ntSteps.ts (step/intent builders, done anchors, retry policy, clarification plumbing: emit-into-payload + answer result + mutable-parent lookup + apply-intents-and-resume), ntTypes.ts (theme field model + structured summary), ntThemeHtml.ts (deterministic theme.html renderer from the summary)
folderLayout.schemas/: t1-plan.schema.json (plan output: known + questions), t3-generate.schema.json (theme.ts string + structured summary)
folderLayout.steps/t1-plan/: readme.md, prompt.md, gate.ts, gate.test.ts, CHANGELOG.md — NO agent file: the plan call is the ROOT's own message call (see treeOverview), so agentNewTheme.ts owns beforePromptImplicit/afterPromptStep for it. A separate agentNtPlan would cost a second cheap LLM round-trip for the same classification.
folderLayout.steps/t2-clarify/: readme.md, agentNtClarify.ts (emits clarification; mounts Decision Clarification), CHANGELOG.md
folderLayout.steps/t3-generate/: readme.md, agentNtGenerate.ts (LLM design; writes + compiles on a green gate; openStepView = read-only Theme Confirmation), prompt.md (injects themeAuthoring), gate.ts, gate.test.ts, CHANGELOG.md
folderLayout.shared (NOT in this folder): l2/aura/molecules/shared/vThemeContract.ts (validator+types), widgetDecisionClarification.* (the checkpoint), widgetThemeConfirmation.* (read-only step view) — see todo Fase 0/4

treeOverview: root (t1-plan, cheap LLM: language + admission + known + questions)
-> t3-generate (design LLM: theme.ts + summary, gated) -> writes theme.ts + theme.html, compiles, t3-done (terminal)
strictly sequential; t3 dependsOn t2-done when the checkpoint ran, else it is the first runnable step

steps.agentName: agentNewTheme (the root itself — no separate step agent)
steps.goal: Cheap classifier. Admission (project has NO l2/skills/theme.ts; else fail readable). Detect userLanguage + a short title. Parse the initial prompt into `known` (the theme fields it could determine) and build `questions` for the CANONICAL fields still missing — CLOSED fields (enums + typography.uppercaseLabels) carry 2-4 options with enum ids and one recommended; OPEN fields (name, primary, border.color, background.css) may carry no options but must set allowNotes. Persist plan.json. If `questions` is empty, plant t3 directly (fast path, no checkpoint); otherwise plant t2 then t3.

checks: output parses to {known, questions[]} with valid field ids/options
questions never repeat a field or re-ask something already in known
CLOSED fields: 2+ options, enum ids, at most one recommended
OPEN fields: options may be empty, but then allowNotes must be true (else the widget could never mark it answered)
gate.onFail: NO retry: fail readable. Admission (no existing theme.ts) is checked EARLIER, in beforePromptImplicit, so it costs no LLM call

steps.doneAnchor: none (the root plants the tree directly)

steps.onlyWhen: plan.questions is non-empty (else this step is not planted — fast path)
steps.goal: THE checkpoint (collect missing fields + the free-text slot). Emit a clarification into this step's own payload; beforeClarificationStep mounts the shared Decision Clarification widget with plan.questions (options + recommended defaults + free-text). On answer, write answers.json to l4 and emit the completed 't2-done' result (the anchor t3-generate dependsOn) carrying the collected values. Cancel => this step fails and the pipeline stops with nothing written.

dependsOn: t2-done (when the checkpoint ran; otherwise none — it is the first runnable step)
steps.goal: THE generation call, and the ONLY writer. prompt.md injects the themeAuthoring meta-skill + the initial prompt + `known` + the checkpoint answers. Output via strict tool schema: the COMPLETE theme.ts (string, contract v1, English comments) + a structured summary (name, displayName, background, palette[], signature[]). On a GREEN gate: persist draft.json, write _<dest>_/l2/skills/theme.ts + theme.html (deterministic renderer from the summary), compile the .ts best-effort, and emit the terminal t3-done anchor with { theme, files[], compiled }. openStepView mounts the shared Theme Confirmation widget in READONLY mode (palette + signature stay inspectable after the fact — it is a view, not a gate).

checks: the generated SOURCE is read statically (parseThemeSource — no eval) and the reconstructed module passes the shared vThemeContract.validateVThemeModule (3 exports, themeInfo fields, suffix starts with '-', 3 mandatory skill sections, examples shape)
raw TypeScript, no markdown fences, no import statements (self-contained data module), skill is one template literal with escaped inner backticks
structured summary present and consistent (name/background identical to themeInfo; palette tokens are --ml-* and declared in the Tokens section)
gate.onFail: retry 1 with gate errors in context; a 2nd failure FAILS the step — nothing is written (the trace carries the errors)

acceptance.regression: none on existing agents beyond the vTheme.ts re-export of the shared validator (agentNewMoleculeVariant suite must stay green)
acceptance.test1: project WITHOUT theme.ts, rich prompt (fast path: no questions) -> writes theme.ts + theme.html, contract valid, compiled
acceptance.test2: project WITHOUT theme.ts, vague prompt -> the checkpoint asks the missing fields with options; answers drive generation
acceptance.test3: cancelling the checkpoint writes nothing; a gate that stays red after the retry writes nothing
acceptance.test4: cycle: run agentNewMoleculeVariant on the freshly created theme (it consumes the new theme.ts) -> a molecule variant is generated
